title: Comparing Keppard, Oliver and Bunk Johnson
summary: Simeon played with Keppard at the Savoy under Charlie Elgar; Keppard had more drive and a bigger tone than Oliver, while Bunk was creative but more subdued.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, I played with Keppard for a while. How did you like him? At the Svobal with Charlie Elgin. Oh, he was a terrific drive, a trumpet player. He was a nice tone.
How did you compare him with Oliver, a different style in Oliver? Well he had a much, he had more drive than Oliver.
Big tone, yeah. Big tone, yeah. And he could play very, very sweet too on his instrument. But he had that drive, you know, big, big, broad tone. More so, I think, than Oliver.
Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
Well, Bunk was creative, but his tone was a little more subdued. He didn't have the drive or power that Keppard or Oliver or Louie had, but he was creative. More and more subdued tone, you know.
